title: Courtyard is out: 14 PSX post-Soviet residents, $7.99
bodyHtml:
Courtyard is out. 14 low poly PS1-style residents of a 1990s post-Soviet apartment block courtyard, rigged and animated for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal: $7.99, with a free sampler on this page.

The cast: a babushka in a headscarf and quilted coat, an old chess player in a flat cap, a lad in a plain tracksuit, a student, a kiosk vendor, a neighbour in a white vest, a taxi driver in a leather jacket, a patrolman in a peaked cap, a postwoman, a plumber, a yard sweeper in an orange quilted jacket, a schoolteacher, a night-shift nurse and a pensioner in a fur hat. Every one an adult, each a different body and painted outfit, about 1,500 triangles and one 256 px texture per skin, three palettes each. No stars, badges, insignia, logos or text anywhere.

Rigged and animated: 45 clips on one standard humanoid skeleton, in GLB, FBX, OBJ and Blender formats, plus our PSX shader for Godot 4. The four hats are modelled geometry.

Tested before release: the pack gate and its break test, a blank Godot 4.7 import of every GLB with the shader compiled under three renderers, and every FBX and OBJ reopened in Blender. The files on this page were compared with our release folder before upload: 145 of 145 identical, and 15 of 15 for the sampler.

Try it free: the sampler on this page is the babushka, with all three skins and every clip. The PSX Character Library holds our PSX packs on one page and takes in every new one; Courtyard joins it in the Library's next update.

Count so far: 26 paid PSX packs; 9 of our PSX pages have sold, 31 purchases in all.

Made with AI tools: the bodies were generated by scripts an AI system wrote, and every texture is an AI image model's painting projected onto the mesh. The skeleton and clips are the CC0 Quaternius Universal Animation Library.
